item.title: Plans to increase Windsor Park capacity to 23,750
item.description: The current capacity of Windsor Park is 18,500 [Getty Images] The planned redevelopment of Windsor Park to enable the stadium to host games at the 2035 Women's World Cup includes proposals to increase the stadium's capacity to 23,750, according to a Fifa report. A joint bid to host the tournament has been submitted by the governing bodies in England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The UK-wide bid is the only one put forward to host the tournament and is therefore set to be ratified at the Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November. Belfast's Windsor Park is the only stadium from Northern Ireland nominated as part of the bid, but in order to comply with the Fifa proposal that it could host games up until the quarter-final stage, the capacity of the venue must be increased from the current 18,500 capacity. The Fifa report said that "further redevelopment is planned, including the increase in capacity" of Windsor Park up to 23,750 by 2035. "These works are expected to enhance the stadium's suitability as a modern international venue," the report continued. "The stadium authority has committed to implementing the necessary upgrades to achieve compliance with the minimum requirements." Alongside the increase in capacity, other parts of the planned redevelopment to Windsor Park include the installation of "a hybrid‑grass system with tournament‑compliant field‑of‑play dimensions" and "an upgrade of the floodlighting system". The Irish Football Association (IFA) has been contacted for comment. The stadium was last redeveloped in 2015, when the IFA received £28.75m from the Northern Ireland Executive to bring the seating capacity up to 18,500. Plans for Northern Ireland to host matches during Euro 2028 fell through after the government said it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament. Windsor Park is one of 19 stadiums that feature in the joint bid for the 2035 World Cup, with 14 based in England, two in Scotland and two in Wales. The English based stadiums included in the bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, City Ground, Stadium of Light and Old Trafford. Easter Road and Hampden Park are the two Scottish stadiums put forward, with Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues. Brazil will host the 2027 Women's World Cup, while the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica made the sole bid for the 2031 tournament. The 2031 edition will be expanded to include 48 teams for the first time, up from 32.

item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Michigan State looks like a national title contender, and Jeremy Fears is the reason why
item.description: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images CHICAGO — Jeremy Fears Jr. was on a mission playing in front of his hometown crowd at the Champions Classic. Led by a brilliant effort from Fears, the National Player of the Year frontrunner, No. 5 Michigan State hit No. 2 Duke hard with the first punch and never relented during a convincing 79-73 victory on Tuesday night. While the opening matchup of college basketball’s annual November showcase looked like it might be one-sided in favor of the Blue Devils — who entered the game as nearly 7-point favorites — the Spartans opened the game on an 11-2 run, never trailed and led by double-digits for stretches of the second half. Fears put forth a strong opening salvo for an awards campaign — finishing with 18 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds while completely overshadowing a beleaguered Blue Devil backcourt. Perhaps most importantly, Michigan State looked like a serious national title contender with Fears receiving plenty of help from a variety of sources on both ends of the floor. The Spartans stood out in multiple ways with its impressive Champions Classic win over Duke. As Tom Izzo stood on the sidelines smiling and winking with Michigan State controlling nearly all 40 minutes, it’s clear the Spartans could be a force this season. Fears elevates his game The redemption arc was clear for Fears entering the Duke matchup at Champions Classic. Facing the Blue Devils in a non-conference game last season at the Breslin Center, Fears went a miserable 0-for-10 in a Michigan State loss — finishing with six points and 13 assists. It would have been natural for Fears to aggressively hunt his own offense early to show Duke (and the nation) how he’s evolved as a player. Instead, Fears leaned into playing his own game, finding his teammates and letting his own offense come to him later. Finishing with only three points in the first half, Fears focused on working the ball to Michigan State’s other weapons, finishing the first 20 minutes with eight assists. In the second half, Fears turned up the pressure attacking and splitting ball screens, often drawing multiple Blue Devil defenders and getting to the free-throw line on a regular basis. item.title: Simon Taufel returns to lead ILT20 match officials' panel for Season 5
item.description: One of cricket's most respected match officials, Australia’s Simon Taufel, will return to lead the match officials’ panel at the ILT20 for a fifth consecutive season. The five-time ICC Umpire of the Year (2004–2008) will be the match referee for the season opener on 21 November at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, where defending champions Desert Vipers take on MI Emirates in a rematch of last season’s final. Taufel will share match referee duties through the season with Roshan Mahanama (52 Tests and 213 ODIs for Sri Lanka). New Zealand’s Chris Brown, and Martin Saggers (three Tests for England) will be the on-field umpires for the opener. Australia’s Paul Wilson will be the third umpire and New Zealand’s Wayne Knights the fourth umpire. Wilson will alternate as third umpire (TV umpire) with West Indies’ Leslie Reifer for the competition. Both have been appointed as specialist TV umpires, with the ILT20 leveraging the HE Smart Replay system to enhance the accuracy and time efficiency of third-umpire decision-making. The panel also includes ICC Elite Panel umpires Richard Illingworth (nine Tests and 25 ODIs for England) and South Africa’s Adrian Holdstock, along with Afghanistan’s Ahmad Pakteen. Aasif Iqbal, Akbar Ali Khan and Shiju Mannil represent the UAE. To help develop officiating in the region, and as part of their wider partnership, the ILT20 will invite two umpires each from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia to shadow the panel during the league stage. They will attend matches to gain first-hand exposure to officiating at a higher level. The programme will be supported by former ICC Umpires Coach Dennis Burns. Ahead of the season, Taufel said: “It’s a privilege to return for a fifth season of the ILT20. We’re strengthened this year by ICC Elite Panel umpires Richard Illingworth and Adrian Holdstock, alongside Roshan Mahanama, talented umpires from across the world, and an ever-improving group of UAE officials. Our focus remains to keep the spotlight on the players and the quality of cricket through officiating excellence.” On the programme for Kuwaiti and Saudi umpires, Taufel added: “Bringing umpires from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia into our environment is a really exciting step for officiating in the region. Working alongside an international panel and learning from someone like Dennis Burns will give them exposure they can take back home and build on.” The updated Season 5 Playing Conditions also take effect from the opening match. The biggest on-field change is a new “batter zone” for judging wides on both sides, and umpires have been told to apply it strictly to stop negative bowling. The 60-second stop clock between overs now applies to the batting side as well. After two warnings in an innings, the fielding side will be awarded five penalty runs. ILT20 Season 5 will feature some of the game’s biggest stars, including Moeen Ali, Usman Tariq and Finn Allen (Abu Dhabi Knight Riders), Babar Azam, Shimron Hetmyer and Naseem Shah (Desert Vipers)

item.description: John Jones-Imagn Images Devils make hugely disappointing Anthony Mantha injury move appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Anthony Mantha signed a two-year, $9.5 million contract with the New Jersey Devils this offseason, and he’s off to a terrific start with five goals and 10 points in 17 games with his new team. But the Devils will be without Mantha for an extended stretch after placing him on long-term injured reserve Wednesday, retroactive to Nov. 7. Mantha took a high stick to the throat from New York Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech during a 5-4 overtime victory on Nov. 7. He returned to Newark for further medical evaluation. He’s put up 10 points this season while averaging just 13:28 of ice time. With an extended absence ahead, New Jersey recalled forwards Lenni Hämeenaho and Stefan Noesen from the American Hockey League’s Utica Comets. Riley Tufte was loaned back to Utica. Mantha’s absence breaks up the third line he shared with Evan Rodrigues and Jesper Boqvist. Arseny Gritsyuk has joined Jesper Bratt and Jack Hughes on New Jersey’s top line and is up to 14 points in 19 games this season. Noesen has appeared in five games for the Devils this year, chipping in three points. He’s also been productive in the AHL, amassing six points in seven games. The 33-year-old was great in his first year back in Newark in 2024-25, recording 41 points and 152 hits in 78 games. As for Hämeenaho, the 22-year-old leads Utica in scoring with six goals and nine points in 11 games and is looking to make his first NHL appearance of the season. He notched eight points in 33 games as a rookie. Things will get more challenging without Mantha, but the Devils have been on a tear , winning nine of their last 11 games to improve to 13-6-0. That has them in second place in the Metropolitan Division, behind only the Carolina Hurricanes (14-3-2). They’re back in action against the visiting Washington Capitals on Thursday night, with puck drop set for just past 7 p.m. ET at the Prudential Center. item.title: Guether Steiner warns Oscar Piastri's McLaren future could be at risk after 2027
item.description: Motorsport photo Former Haas Formula 1 team principal Guenther Steiner has warned that Oscar Piastri could find his McLaren future under threat if he has another season like 2026. Piastri, who fought for the world title in 2025, has endured a much tougher campaign this time around and is out of the fight for second in the championship with three rounds to go. item.description: wwe Killer Kross and WWE have not held any formal talks about a return, according to PWInsider . After Kross lost the MLW World Heavyweight Championship, talk spread that Kross had wrapped up his MLW run and was bound for WWE NXT. PWInsider’s Mike Johnson shot that down, reporting that the two sides have not had any formal discussions. Johnson added that Kross is still part of the MLW roster. He is not under an exclusive contract, so he can take bookings with MLW, Australia’s WSW or any other company that he and his wife, Scarlett Bordeaux, want to work with. Kross lost the MLW title to Josh Bishop in a Last Man Standing match at MLW Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7. The two brawled through the crowd with tables, chairs, and a bat, and Bishop won by putting Kross through a table with his Exit 187. Kross tried to use a chair to get back to his feet, but Bishop kicked it out from under him, and Kross could not answer the 10-count. The loss ended a reign of 283 days. Kross won the title by winning the Battle Riot match at MLW Battle Riot VIII in January and made seven successful defenses as champion. He also added the WSW Championship in Australia in May, beating Bishop Dyer for the vacant title. Kross and Scarlett left WWE in August 2025 when their contracts expired. Kross later said WWE did not make him an offer until shortly before his deal expired, gave him 24 hours to accept after he asked how the company arrived at the number, and then pulled the offer. Scarlett was not offered a new contract. Killer Kross Is Better Off as a Free Agent Kross had two stints with WWE. He became a two-time NXT Champion during his first run, winning the title from Keith Lee at NXT TakeOver XXX in 2020, vacating it because of a shoulder injury, and winning it back from Finn Balor at NXT TakeOver: Stand & Deliver in 2021. WWE released him in November 2021 before bringing him back in August 2022 as Karrion Kross, when he began a feud with Drew McIntyre on SmackDown. He later led the Final Testament faction with Scarlett, Paul Ellering and the Authors of Pain. After leaving WWE, Kross returned to MLW in November 2025 by beating Matt Riddle. Kross has done more for his career since leaving WWE than he did in his final years there. item.title: Mike Tomlin Reveals Why He Stepped Down From Coaching the Steelers
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin after a game against the New York Jets on Sep. 7, 2025 -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin opened up to Cam Heyward on why he stepped down as the Steelers HC after 19 seasons in January. Tomlin said he knew he was done shortly after the Wild Card round loss to the Houston Texans. “I did probably by the time I pulled in my driveway,” Tomlin explained when asked if he knew he was going to walk away right the loss to Houston. “Football, man, is bigger than all of us, and I never took myself so seriously that I thought that I was immune from that. I never wanted to stay too long. As a football lover, I was always really impressed by those that moved away or had the self-awareness to move away at what they deemed the appropriate time. I just always wanted to respect the game enough to be able to do that. To not overstay my welcome. That was a big component of me coming to the decision as anything.” View this post on Instagram The Steelers lost seven straight playoff games under Tomlin. The franchise’s last playoff win was on Jan. 15, 2017 against the Kansas City Chiefs. “I just thought we had the makings of a really good team, a team that is capable of competing for and winning a championship,” Tomlin said. “But when I really started thinking about it, man, my bags might slow that down. I thought that guys like [Heyward] and T.J. [Watt] were deserving of the optimism that comes with new regimes. I’ve been around that. I saw it in Tampa. I want that for those guys, even if it means it doesn’t happen with me.” Related Headlines Steelers CB Jalen Ramsey Has Clear Message for Ja’Marr Chase Bengals Get Major Reinforcements for Steelers Game Bill Cowher, Former Steelers Players Pay Tribute to Dick Hoak Read more at Steelers Now

item.title: Rumor Suggests NY Yankees May Be Making Big Mistake By Letting Jazz Chisholm Leave in Free Agency
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the large majority of New York Yankees fans welcome the idea of moving on from infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr., a new rumor may suggest that letting him walk in MLB free agency is a mistake. There is no doubt that Chisholm Jr. has talent. He is a two-time All-Star who has a legit power bat and the rare skill set to be a 30-30 (home runs and stolen bases) player when he is hitting on all cylinders. Furthermore, he is a versatile fielder who can play multiple positions on the infield and outfield and is still in his 20s. There is also no doubt that he can be a locker room problem. The Yankees knew that when they traded for him two years ago. But it was worth the risk because of his talent. However, his immaturity, lack of focus on defense, and a down season in 2026 have soured opinions about him among New York fans. Yet, despite the obvious red flags in his character and baseball skills, it seems that Chisholm Jr. has fast become one of the most sought-after players in free agency. According to MLB Network’s Jon Morosi, eleven teams are in discussions with Chisholm Jr.’s representatives , and “multiple in-person meetings are being scheduled next week.” If nearly a dozen teams are interested in the 28-year-old, are the Yankees making the wrong move by letting him walk? Are the New York Yankees making a mistake by letting Jazz Chisholm walk? Sep 30, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) reacts after hitting a single in the second inning against the Boston Red Sox during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images If the Yankees let Chisholm Jr. leave, they have a hole at second base that won’t be easily filled — whether you like him or not. While they have been linked to free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe, the word around the team is that they are more likely to address 2B internally with either Anthony Volpe or Luis Garcia Jr. Volpe is not a problem child and is a solid player, but he can’t create big moments like Chisholm Jr., and it is debatable whether he will be better defensively. Garcia Jr. is absolutely a better hitter, but there is a reason the Washington Nationals moved him from second to first base. A case could certainly be made that, with a different manager or stronger leadership in the clubhouse, the negative parts of Chisholm Jr.’s personality could be held in check, so his positive energy and passion could be a huge plus for the team. Yet, neither is coming in 2027. That is why the Yankees are not making a mistake by letting the infielder take his talents elsewhere. Nevertheless, it is still very interesting that so many teams want the player New York fans have grown tired of. item.title: IndyCar 2026 season review: ECR
item.description: Motorsport photo The 2026 IndyCar Series season was a year of elevated expectations, persistent growing pains, and missed opportunities for ECR. Entering the second full campaign under the strengthened ownership structure backed by Heartland Food Products Group founder Ted Gelov, the Indianapolis-based outfit aimed to build on the momentum of Christian Rasmussen ’s breakthrough 2025 Milwaukee victory and convert its off-track investments into consistent front-running execution. Instead, the 18-race schedule turned into an uphill battle against mid-pack attrition, mechanical setbacks, and Sunday execution woes. Alexander Rossi returned for his second season anchoring the #20 Chevrolet, hoping to turn strong single-lap pace into sustained frontrunning contention. While the 2016 Indianapolis 500 winner regularly flashed top-10 speed – highlighted by an impressive front-row qualifying effort for the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 – trouble repeatedly found him on race days. There was also the notable terrifying high-speed accident in Monday practice ahead of the Indy 500, where Rossi lost control in Turn 2 and suffered a heavy impact with the SAFER barrier before being collected by Arrow McLaren ’s Pato O'Ward , sustaining injuries to his right ankle and a finger on his left hand that required surgery. Displaying trademark grit, Rossi returned to take the start on Sunday, though the team's entire Indianapolis campaign was derailed; he finished 30th in the race after a mechanical issue. Outside of Indianapolis, Rossi endured what he candidly termed a "pretty terrible year" through the bulk of the calendar, plagued by more mechanical retirements, pit-lane setbacks, and mid-pack contact. However, the 34-year-old salvaged a strong closing race, capping off the campaign with his first podium since 2024 – and his first in ECR colors – by driving to a gritty third-place finish in the season finale at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. That late surge lifted Rossi to 15th in the final championship standings with 307 points, courtesy of that podium alongside five top-10 finishes. item.description: Oct 7, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees right fielder Aaron Judge (99) against the Tampa Bay Rays in game three of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Judge got a good report on his rib. That buys the Yankees some peace of mind this winter. It shouldn’t buy the front office a pass on adding another hitter it can put in the top half of the order. Brian Cashman told reporters there was no new procedure planned after Judge’s follow-up on his right rib fracture, Bryan Hoch reported . A September calf strain also cost him time. The club is encouraged by the recovery, which is different from knowing how many games he’ll play next season. Oct 3, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge (99) looks on from the dugout before game one of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What a healthy Judge can’t fix for the Yankees Judge still had an .871 OPS and 18 homers in 66 games. The team finished with a .311 on-base percentage, and Ben Rice was its only 20-homer hitter . There is a hole between getting the captain back and fielding a lineup that can score through a week when he isn’t carrying it. I’d shop for an everyday bat with a history of getting on base, not a bench player whose biggest selling point is that he can stand in right field. That hitter can play in the infield or the outfield. The point is to give the order another at-bat opponents have to work through, whether Judge is in the lineup or getting the day off. The cheaper plan is to trust the returning bats and spend most of the budget on pitching. There’s a case for that with bullpen jobs open, and .311 isn’t a forecast for next year. But buying a little coverage for the roster isn’t the same as buying a hitter good enough to move up the order. I’d make the latter a priority before the market dictates which positions are left. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. item.title: Knicks can put OG Anunoby on the ball before the screen
item.description: Nov 10, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks forward Og Anunoby (8) looks to drive past Milwaukee Bucks guard Brayden Burries (0) in the third quarter at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Harden hit five of seven threes against the Knicks on Wednesday. The number I wouldn’t overlook is 11. That’s how many free throws he took on his way to 32 points, and it’s why simply chasing the next guard farther out isn’t much of a plan. OG Anunoby had two steals and a block in 34 minutes. That doesn’t say how often he guarded Harden or whose assignment broke down. It does give New York a defender worth using earlier in the action, before the next ball handler decides which matchup he wants. How the Knicks can use Anunoby before the screen I’d try switching Anunoby onto the ball handler before the screen arrives on a few possessions in Friday’s Cup game at Indiana . Then keep the big close enough to discourage the pull-up without leaving the lane empty. Starting the action with length at the point of attack is a better option than asking a smaller guard to recover from behind while the big has to pick between a shooter and a roll man. Nov 7, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby (8) defends Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (45) in the fourth quarter at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The alternative is a deeper drop with the original defender chasing over the screen. It protects the rim and makes sense when the ball handler isn’t a pull-up threat. If Indiana starts hunting that space, though, New York should change the matchup before the screen, not wait until both defenders are reacting to the ball. Harden’s shooting isn’t going to carry over to a different opponent. The choice he presented is still there. Give Anunoby a chance to take away the first read instead of asking him to clean up the second. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. item.title: Missouri State women's basketball eyes big test versus Marquette
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State (3-0) intends on using last year’s experience this season. That is why the Lady Bears’ upcoming game is a major early test of the season. Missouri State hosts Marquette (2-1) at 6:30 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 13. Last season, the Lady Bears entered the NCAA Tournament as the No. 16 seed. Looking back, the team knows that a few key non-conference wins could’ve helped their postseason seeding. “If we would have just won at least one of our tougher games, we could’ve have gotten a better seeding,” Lainie Douglas said. “That lights a fire under our butt to win a few of these games and make it to the tournament and get a higher seeding.” Missouri State: Lady Bears find defensive rhythm early behind transfer Hannah Linthacum Marquette has finished above .500 in every season since 2017. The Golden Eagles have also won at least 18 games since that mark, too. They have reached the NCAA Tournament six times in the last 10 years. It’s safe to say this is a big game for the Lady Bears. Not only is it difficult to schedule big-time opponents in today's college basketball landscape, but it’s also even harder to host big games. “The non-conference schedule is a good opportunity to show how talented we are,” Douglas said. Missouri State is off to a flying start with blowout wins over Southeast Missouri State, Wyoming, and Wichita State. The Lady Bears have shown an identity of stifling defense and efficiency inside the lane. It doesn’t matter the opponent, good defense and consistent scoring will always translate to wins. Marquette’s lone loss came against No. 17 Minnesota in an 87-79 defeat. The Lady Bears will also play against the Golden Gophers in the Cancun Challenge on Thursday, Nov. 26. Missouri State soccer: Bears eliminated from American tournament, awaits postseason bid While Kaemyn Bekemeier leads the Lady Bears, Marquette’s Halle Vice is its star player. The 6-foot-1 senior was an all-Big East First Team member last season. She was also picked to the preseason All-Big East Team list. Vice has scored at least 12 points in every game, including a 25-point outburst against Minnesota. She can hit deep 3-pointers while scoring inside. She’s a true matchup threat for any team she faces. Missouri State’s defense has been spectacular to start. The Lady Bears are allowing just 29% of their opponents to hit shots this season. Interior defense led by Douglas and Hannah Linthacum could be a major key in this game. A win over Marquette will not only give Missouri State confidence moving forward, but it will also be huge for the team’s RPI down the road. Marquette will be bound to pick up some big wins across the season. The Golden Eagles still have to face Wisconsin and Illinois, along with two games against national championship contender UConn and several other Big East powers. Craig Melvin , Al Roker and Dylan Dreyer announced Hicks’ death at age 64 during the third hour of Today on Thursday, Nov. 12, as Melvin got visibly emotional reflecting on the life of their NBC colleague. Melvin honored the sports broadcaster as a “dear friend and beloved member of our NBC family.” After Dreyer detailed Hicks’ resumé, Roker added that he was “more importantly” a “devoted” father and husband. item.title: Did anyone actually compare Austin Reaves to Larry Bird?
item.description: One of the most-clicked stories on The Big Lead right now is about Charles Barkley going off on some poor fool on the Detroit Pistons broadcast comparing Austin Reaves to Larry Bird. Barkley, who is honestly one of the top-five sports television talents to ever don a lavalier, obviously constructed an entertaining rant. The footage has been posted all over the internet and, positively, it has given fans yet another reason to search out Bird highlights, which are permanently electric. MORE: Charles Barkley drops multiple expletives in Larry Bird-Austin Reaves rant Over and over I read that the Pistons broadcast had compared Reaves, who is having a tremendous year for the Los Angeles Lakers, to Bird. Curiosity took over—because this made no sense—and led to a more detailed search about what exactly was said. Like, how in the world would a comment like that even make air? What the heck happened? Well, as it turns out, no one compared Reaves to Bird as a player. At all. Here’s what happened. Early in the game, Reaves made a sick shot while falling behind the basket. Longtime Pistons analyst Greg Kelser, former teammate of Magic Johnson on Michigan State’s 1979 national title-winning team, realized that the fall-away shot was reminscent of a classic Bird clip. item.title: Warriors reveal Stephen Curry injury diagnosis after MRI on abdomen
item.description: The Golden State Warriors were already without one star. Now they’ll be without their Most Valuable Player candidate, Stephen Curry , for the short-term future, too. The Warriors announced Thursday, Nov. 12 that an MRI confirmed Curry suffered an oblique abdominal tear and added that he would be reevaluated in two weeks. The injury took place Wednesday, Nov. 11 in an eventual 115-108 loss against the Houston Rockets . Curry walked off the floor midway through the first quarter, clearly grimacing and favoring his right side. The sequence took place just 5:35 into the game. Curry had scored 3 points on 1-of-3 shooting by that point. He did not return to the floor for the rest of the first quarter, and he was not back at the bench area to start the second period. ANALYSIS: What does Curry injury mean for Warriors? Can they weather the storm? The Warriors announced minutes into the second quarter that Curry would not return for the rest of the game with right abdominal soreness. After the game, Warriors coach Steve Kerr said that Curry said he “tweaked something in his abdominal area,” which Curry told Kerr he had never done before. Kerr added that “concern is high” though he reiterated that he had no idea of the extent of the injury. During the game, Curry did have a collision with Rockets forward Amen Thompson earlier in the game, when Curry had driven to the hoop on an attempted layup. Then, Curry had been fighting off a screen against Rockets center Alperen Şengün. As soon as that sequence ended, Curry once again grabbed his side. Finally, just moments before he left the game, Curry curled around a screen and put up a 3-point shot. As soon as he landed and stepped backwards, he grabbed at his right side, near his hip. Curry had been in the midst of a renaissance and had been elevating the play of the Warriors, who entered Wednesday night 8-3, which was tied for the third best record in the Western Conference . Prior to suffering the injury, Curry was averaging 30.6 points, 4.1 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game in nine appearances. He was converting 3-pointers at a blistering 45.7%, which would mark a career-high. His scoring total entering Wednesday night had ranked second in the NBA, behind only Luka Dončić’s historic 39.3 points per game, for all players with at least five games played. The Warriors were already without Jimmy Butler, who has missed the start of the season as he rehabs the torn anterior cruciate ligament he suffered in January 2026. According to the Manchester Evening News, Pochettino will leave the US after the second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati, which is set to finish at around 2am UK time next Wednesday. He is then expected to reach Manchester later that day and begin his duties at Carrington next Thursday. Three days to prepare for Liverpool That timeline would give Pochettino just three days with his new squad before United travel to Anfield to face Liverpool next Sunday. BBC Sport also reports that he is likely to be in his post by November 19 at the latest. United have agreed personal terms with the Argentine and have reportedly established a framework with US Soccer to buy him out of his four-year contract, which contains a £7.4 million release clause. He is also expected to bring several members of his long-standing backroom staff with him to Old Trafford. Pochettino to face media before Haiti double-header United and US Soccer have agreed that Pochettino will oversee both games against Haiti before ending his time in charge of the national team. He is due to speak to the media at the US training base just outside Atlanta at 2.15pm (UK time) on Friday, before the first leg kicks off in Kingston, Jamaica, at 9.30pm on Saturday. The 54-year-old has won 21 of his 35 matches as USMNT boss and led them into the World Cup knockout stages earlier this year, before a round-of-16 exit against Belgium. Anfield debut awaits Pochettino Pochettino will return to English football with plenty of Premier League experience, having previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, as well as Paris Saint-Germain. His first task will be to lift a struggling United side at Anfield next Sunday, with very little time to work with his players.
